Scholar Diana Walsh Pasulka joins Danny Jones to say that top space scientists suspect UFOs are Bible-era time machines. Pasulka studies how UFO belief works like a faith. Her books draw on talks with scientists who work in secret programs.

Pasulka explains why smart people in space work treat the craft as more than nuts and bolts. She ties their views to old texts and to time itself. Jones asks how a craft could move through time and what that would mean for faith. Listeners get a scholar's view of a wild claim. The library files the talk as an archive record.

Geneticist David Sinclair joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1349 to present his science of aging. Sinclair, a Harvard researcher, argues that aging is a loss of information in our cells, and that it can be slowed or partly reversed. His book made the claim a public debate.

He walks Rogan through the lab work, from yeast and mice to the human trials then under way. Rogan asks what Sinclair himself takes and does each day. The episode is a clear brief for the longevity field's boldest hope, delivered by its most famous advocate, with the caveats a good host draws out.
